thread:
alex: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection tweak landed last night we're seeing a scaling regression on 8-node TP clusters. Jobs hit a sudden all-reduce spike and some runs timeout (>60s write barrier).
priya: Yikes. Is this the change that prefers fused matmul kernels for short sequences?
alex: Yeah. The selector favored the new small-M fused kernel when avg_seq_len < 32. Good on single-node, but multi-node latency blows up.
sam: Do we have profiles? NCCL traces or timeline?
alex: Yes — I grabbed a perf.trace from a 8xA10 run. Top-level: all-reduce latency increases roughly linearly with ranks and stalls during KV restore. Flame graph attached (pasted snippets):
```
# timeline slice
0.000 - 0.120s compute (forward)
0.120 - 0.410s allreduce(kv-cache) blocking
0.410 - 0.500s compute (backward)
```

marta: That blocking window is huge. Looks like we lost comm/compute overlap because the compute kernels became too fast (smaller GEMMs) so the ordering causes sync points to wait for slow NVLink rings.
alex: Exactly. The micro-kernel finishes early and then issues a blocking all-reduce for the KV update. On larger sequence lengths the kernel is slower so overlap masks the all-reduce cost.
priya: Any config workaround? Could we relax the selector threshold to prefer the previous kernel for TP > 1 or when num_ranks > 4?
sam: We can gate selector with a topology-aware rule. If world_size > 1 and avg_batch_tokens per GPU < X, force slower but better-overlapped kernel.
priya: Also seeing KV cache size churn — some ranks call restore earlier causing rank skew. That can exacerbate NCCL barriers (rendezvous mismatch).
infra-bot: deploy: rollout start 1769234600 — regression-rollback patch queued.
marta: Quick mitigation: change batching heuristic to increase micro-batch depth so compute time > comm latency. For example, accumulate 2 micro-batches before KV flush.
alex: I prototyped a flag: --tp-comm-mode=async-kv which posts all-reduce as background non-blocking and postpones the barrier until end-of-layer. That reduced wall-time by ~35% in local sim, but risks increased memory spikes.
sam: Need test across 2,4,8 nodes. Also run with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO to capture timeline.
priya: Can we reproduce deterministically? I can try a synthetic profile harness with controlled seq_len distribution.
alex: Please do. Use seed 42 and seq_len mix [8:0.6, 24:0.3, 64:0.1]. The regression shows up in that mix.
sam: If async-kv looks promising we should add a safety fallback: if any rank lags >500ms defer to blocking mode and trigger telemetry.
marta: Agreed. Also log per-rank KV restore timestamps to help detect skew. Small change to runtime: emit `kv_restore_ts` metric per step.
priya: Work items: 1) temporary rollback to old kernel selector (infra patch queued), 2) add topology-aware selector rule, 3) prototype async-kv + memory guard, 4) synthetic harness runs + NCCL traces.
alex: Assigning: priya->synthetic harness + traces, sam->async-kv prototype, marta->metrics + selector rule. I'll monitor rollback.
priya: On it. Posting first trace in #eng-runtime after a run.
alex: Thanks — let's sync in 2 hours. :hourglass:
